title: Conspiracy Narratives in the Protest Movement Against COVID-19 Restrictions in Germany. A Long-term Content Analysis of Telegram Chat Groups.
screen_reason: Automated content analysis of 821,903 text messages sent between 29 April 2020 and 29 May 2022 in 34 public Querdenken Telegram chat groups. Four experts annotated 4,863 messages (intercoder kappa 0.82) for whether a message shows signs of a conspiracy narrative, a fine-tuned DistilBERT model was trained on those labels and applied to the whole corpus, and the paper's RQ1 is explicitly prevalence: 67,698 messages, 8.24% of the corpus, were classified as containing conspiracy narratives. That is a share of items in a defined corpus judged against an expert-defined content standard, so CONTENT. Marked borderline because the label is 'signs of conspiracy narratives' rather than verified falsity.

estimates.country: Germany (Querdenken movement, mainly Southern Germany; East German groups largely absent)
estimates.measure_type: % of Telegram messages in Querdenken protest chat groups classified as containing signs of conspiracy narratives
estimates.value_raw: our trained model identified 67,698 messages containing characteristics of conspiracy narratives, representing 8.24% of the total corpus (of 821,903 messages)
estimates.denominator: 821,903 text messages exchanged in 34 public Querdenken Telegram chat groups (over one million crawled; messages containing only a video, image or link removed)
estimates.definition: A message counted for the numerator if the fine-tuned classifier assigned the label 'shows signs of conspiracy narratives'; in the human guidelines a message is labelled 1 when it clearly indicates signs of conspiracy narratives or matches a guiding question (secret organizations influencing political decisions, leaders as puppets, the government using COVID-19 to monitor and control people, the government concealing the truth, COVID-19 orchestrated by evil actors); ambiguous or merely conspiracy-adjacent terminology is labelled 0
estimates.misinfo_def: "conspiracy narratives are beliefs and convictions that attempt to interpret historical and contemporary events and general societal changes as a conspiracy and/or secret plan by a group of powerful actors"
estimates.source_quote: Concerning the prevalence of conspiracy narra- tives (RQ1), our trained model identified 67,698 messages containing characteristics of conspiracy narratives, representing 8.24% of the total corpus.
estimates.page_loc: Section 4 'Temporal analysis', p. 54 (the 'narra- tives' break is the PDF's line-break hyphenation); the Abstract states 'we find that 8.24% of the sent messages contain signs of conspiracy narratives.'
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Four experts hand-labelled 4,863 messages against written guidelines; each expert also labelled the same 100 random messages, giving an intercoder kappa of 0.82. A DistilBERT model (fine-tuned from distilbert-base-german-cased-toxic-comments) trained on those labels was applied to the full corpus; 5-fold cross-validation gave macro F1 0.851 and, for the conspiracy class, F1 0.757 (SD 0.017), recall 0.692, precision 0.837.
estimates.moderator_quote: We use all public chat groups that are advertised on a page of the main initiative. ... We use all public chat groups of the local Querdenken initiatives linked on the initiative's directory on May 1, 2022 ... We crawled over one million messages sent between 29.04.2020 and 29.05.2022. Since we focus on text messages, messages that contain only a video, an image or a link have been removed with regular expressions. Resulting in a corpus of 821,903 messages that were exchanged in 34 groups.
estimates.notes: borderline=true on the construct: the label is 'shows signs of conspiracy narratives', an expert-defined narrative category, not a claim-by-claim falsity verdict against an external ground truth - though the guiding questions and the example messages (Deep State, Plandemie, Great Reset, forced vaccination to maximise deaths) are canonical false COVID conspiracy claims. Denominator note: the corpus is a self-selected activist community (protest organising groups), not a platform-representative sample, so this is prevalence WITHIN a movement, not on Telegram generally, and it is not comparable to platform-wide estimates. Classifier recall for the conspiracy class is only 0.692 (precision 0.837), so the automated 8.24% probably understates the human-label rate. year set to 2021 as the midpoint of the 25-month collection window (April 2020 - May 2022); the share is not static - the paper reports it rising over time, 'peaking at values around 20%' after February 2022, read off Figure 1 rather than printed, so only the corpus-wide point is rowed per the collapse-the-time-series rule.

missed_or_uncertain: 1) The rising time trend is described but never printed as dated values: 'a further increase has been noticeable since February 2022 peaking at values around 20%' is an eyeballed figure reading, so no time-point rows were made; the corpus-wide 8.24% is the representative point. 2) Volume figures (average 1,080 messages/day overall, 89 conspiracy messages/day, about 457 messages/day in April 2022) are counts, not shares. 3) STM topic prevalences (T5 21.8%, T3 12.8%, T9 12.8%, T7 10.1%, T1/T6/T4 9.1%, T10 6.9%, T8 5.4%, T2 2.8%) are shares of topical content WITHIN the conspiracy-message subset, i.e. a breakdown of the numerator by narrative type rather than a prevalence share; they would qualify as within_misinfo_content material if the review wanted narrative composition, but they are topic proportions from a topic model, not falsity shares, so nothing was rowed. 4) Classifier performance metrics (F1, precision, recall) are instrument properties, not estimates.

rob.design: Automated content analysis of a curated census of public Telegram chat groups. Frame: all public chat groups of local Querdenken initiatives listed on the movement's own directory (app.querdenken-711.de) on 1 May 2022, 34 groups, collected via Telethon on the official Telegram API; over one million messages crawled 29 April 2020 - 29 May 2022, reduced to 821,903 after dropping media/link-only messages. Only timestamp and text retained (no user data). Coding: four expert annotators labelled 4,863 messages with written guidelines and a shared 100-message reliability set (kappa 0.82); the best of several supervised models (fine-tuned DistilBERT, chosen over SVM and Naive Bayes) was trained on all annotated data and applied to the remaining corpus; 5-fold cross-validation, macro F1 0.851, conspiracy-class recall 0.692 and precision 0.837. Known limitations: East German protest groups outside the Querdenken label are excluded; the sample is an activist community rather than a platform sample; no confidence intervals or classification-error correction is applied to the 8.24%; info channels (broadcast-only) were not included, only open chat groups.
rob.item6_quote: A message is annotated as showing signs of conspiracy (annotated as 1) if it clearly indicates signs of conspiracy narratives (see Appendix B for details). A message is annotated as not showing signs of conspiracy (annotated as 0), if no terminology related to know conspiracy is used or the coder cannot determine if the message contains signs of conspiracy narratives.
rob.item10_quote: Concerning the prevalence of conspiracy narratives (RQ1), our trained model identified 67,698 messages containing characteristics of conspiracy narratives, representing 8.24% of the total corpus.
